title: Connection and error states
one_line: Reconnecting, opponent left, no network, maintenance. The screens nobody designs and every player eventually sees - handle them once, everywhere.

anatomy.spec: A small persistent banner/toast (bible 5.20), not a full takeover, that appears when connectivity drops and clears when it returns.
In a match: a semi-transparent overlay over the board with a spinner and 'Reconnecting...'. The board and cards stay visible dimmed underneath - never hide the game state.
A toast: '{NAME} left the match.' If it breaks the match below the minimum player count, offer to continue with a bot filling the seat (labelled BOT) or end the match honestly with a partial result.
A full takeover, mascot, one line explaining what is down and roughly when it will be back, no dead ends - always a way to at least reach Settings/Support.
A full takeover blocking play, UPDATE button to the store listing.

states: No network (extended - match cannot continue, offer to leave without penalty)
motion: Toast slides down under the top bar, 2.2 s hold (bible 5.20), or persists while the condition holds.
Reconnecting spinner: the tumbling six-pip die (bible 5.23).
data: Network reachability, session/match connection state from the eventual online layer (T-D2/T-D3). Client version check against a remote config minimum version.
do_not: Do not let a dropped connection silently forfeit a match - an extended outage must offer to leave without losing the stake, since it was not the player's fault.
Do not hide the board during a brief reconnect - dim it, do not hide it.
Do not design this only for the online path and forget local/bot matches can still hit device-level issues (backgrounding, low memory).
acceptance: Every state in 'states' has a built screen or overlay.
A dropped connection through no fault of the player's does not forfeit the stake.
Version-too-old blocks play cleanly with a working UPDATE button.
steps: 1. Preflight - this is genuinely cross-cutting; coordinate with match-hud.json and the eventual T-D2/T-D3 online work rather than building in isolation.
2. Build the toast for brief no-network.
3. Build the reconnecting overlay for mid-match drops, dimming not hiding the board.
4. Build the opponent-left toast and the bot-fill-or-end-honestly branch.
5. Build the maintenance and version-too-old full takeovers.
6. Wire the no-penalty-leave path for extended outages.
prompt:
Build the Ludo NX connection and error states - the screens nobody designs and every player eventually sees.

Read SCREEN_PLANS/specs/SHARED_RULES.md, SCREEN_PLANS/specs/MATCH_HUD_V2.md, UI_BIBLE/LUDO_NX_UI_BIBLE.md sections 5.20, 5.22 and 5.23, and this whole file. Use only values from UI_BIBLE/tokens.json.

This does not exist yet, as a single cross-cutting system: a brief toast for a dropped connection that clears when it returns; a reconnecting overlay mid-match that DIMS the board rather than hiding it, so the player can see the position they are returning to; a toast plus a bot-fill-or-honest-partial-result branch when an opponent leaves mid-match; a full-takeover maintenance screen with a mascot and an honest timeframe; and a full-takeover version-too-old block with a working UPDATE button to the store listing.

The rule that protects the player: an extended outage that is not their fault must let them leave WITHOUT losing their stake - never let a connection drop silently forfeit a match.

Follow the 'steps' array. Finish with bible section 11 and the 'acceptance' list, with a capture of every state listed.
